question.worked_solution:
The indicator function $1[P]$ equals $1$ if the predicate $P$ is true and $0$ if $P$ is false.

$$
1[P]=\{\begin{aligned}1, & \text{if }P\text{ is true}, \\ 0, & \text{if }P\text{ is false}.\end{aligned}
$$

The expression $1[{x}_{i}>0]\cdot {x}_{i}$ equals ${x}_{i}$ when ${x}_{i}>0$ and equals $0$ otherwise. Thus, the sum 

$$
{\sum }_{i=1}^{5}1[{x}_{i}>0]\cdot {x}_{i}
$$

adds up only the positive values.

We evaluate the indicator function for each ${x}_{i}:$

- $1[{x}_{1}>0]=1[0>0]=0$

- $1[{x}_{2}>0]=1[-7>0]=0$

- $1[{x}_{3}>0]=1[8>0]=1$

- $1[{x}_{4}>0]=1[9>0]=1$

- $1[{x}_{5}>0]=1[-2>0]=0$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{i=1}^{5}1[{x}_{i}>0]\cdot {x}_{i} & =0\cdot 0+0\cdot (-7)+1\cdot 8+1\cdot 9+0\cdot (-2) \\  & =0+0+8+9+0 \\  & =17.\end{aligned}
$$
